title: Psalms Chapter 102 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 102 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 102 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 102.

questions.question: In Psalms 102, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'A Prayer of the afflicted' is the very first line of the chapter, indicating the context of the psalmist's plea to God.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do with his prayer?
options: Let my cry come unto thee
Hide not thy face from me
questions.correctAnswer: Let my cry come unto thee
questions.explanation: The psalmist specifically asks the LORD to 'let my cry come unto thee' in Psalms 102:1.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request in the day of trouble?
options: Hide not thy face from me
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks the LORD to 'answer me speedily' in Psalms 102:2 when he calls in trouble.

questions.question: What metaphor does the psalmist use to describe his days?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that 'my days are consumed like smoke' in Psalms 102:3.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his heart?
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes his heart as 'smitten, and withered like grass' in Psalms 102:4.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about his bones due to his groaning?
options: They are burned as an hearth
questions.explanation: In Psalms 102:5, the psalmist mentions that 'my bones cleave to my skin' because of his groaning.

questions.question: Which bird does the psalmist compare himself to?
questions.explanation: The psalmist likens himself to a 'pelican of the wilderness' in Psalms 102:6.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's state when he watches?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states he 'am as a sparrow alone upon the house top' in Psalms 102:7.

questions.question: What do the psalmist's enemies do to him?
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions that 'mine enemies reproach me all the day' in Psalms 102:8.

questions.question: What has the psalmist eaten like bread?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'For I have eaten ashes like bread' in Psalms 102:9.

questions.question: What caused the psalmist's sorrow according to the text?
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions 'Because of thine indignation and thy wrath' in Psalms 102:10 as the cause of his sorrow.

questions.question: The psalmist is overwhelmed and pours out his complaint before the LORD.
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in Psalms 102:1, where it mentions the psalmist's prayer of the afflicted.

questions.question: The psalmist feels joy and peace throughout the chapter.
questions.explanation: This is incorrect; the psalmist expresses sorrow and anguish throughout the chapter.

questions.question: The psalmist's bones are described as cleaving to his skin.
questions.explanation: While the psalmist does mention his bones cleaving to his skin, he does not say they are described in a positive light.

questions.question: The psalmist asks the LORD to lift him up and cast him down.
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions being lifted up and cast down but does not request this; instead, he is expressing his distress.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 102 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 102 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the psalmist compare his days to in Psalms 102:11?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that 'My days are like a shadow that declineth' in Psalms 102:11, illustrating the fleeting nature of life.

questions.question: What does Psalms 102:12 promise will happen if someone acknowledges the enduring nature of the LORD?
options: They will prosper in all things
They will be comforted in trouble
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:12 emphasizes that 'But thou, O LORD, shalt endure for ever; and thy remembrance unto all generations,' indicating God’s eternal nature and remembrance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 102:13 indicate God will do for Zion?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:13 states, 'Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Zion,' showing God's intention to show compassion.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'stones' of Zion mentioned in Psalms 102:14?
options: They are a source of pleasure for God's servants
They represent the enemies of Zion
questions.correctAnswer: They are a source of pleasure for God's servants
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:14 says, 'For thy servants take pleasure in her stones,' indicating the value and beauty of Zion’s place to God's people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 102:15, what will the heathen do when they see the glory of the LORD?
options: Fear the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Fear the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:15 states, 'So the heathen shall fear the name of the LORD,' reflecting the awe and reverence due to God’s glory.

questions.question: What does Psalms 102:16 say will happen when the LORD builds up Zion?
options: He shall appear in his glory
questions.correctAnswer: He shall appear in his glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:16 declares, 'When the LORD shall build up Zion, he shall appear in his glory,' emphasizing God's presence and power.

questions.question: What assurance is given in Psalms 102:17 regarding the prayers of the destitute?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:17 states, 'He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer,' assuring that God listens to the needy.

questions.question: What does Psalms 102:18 say will be written for future generations?
options: The words of the psalmist's prayer
The praise of the LORD by created people
questions.correctAnswer: The praise of the LORD by created people
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:18 mentions, 'This shall be written for the generation to come: and the people which shall be created shall praise the LORD,' highlighting the importance of praise across generations.

questions.question: From where does the LORD look down according to Psalms 102:19?
options: From the depths of the sea
From the height of his sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: From the height of his sanctuary
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:19 states, 'For he hath looked down from the height of his sanctuary; from heaven did the LORD behold the earth,' indicating God's omniscience and oversight.

questions.question: What does Psalms 102:20 say is the purpose of the LORD hearing the groaning of the prisoner?
options: To loose those that are appointed to death
questions.correctAnswer: To loose those that are appointed to death
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:20 states, 'To hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death,' showing God's intent to deliver and free.

questions.question: If someone is overwhelmed and pours out their complaint before the LORD, what does Psalms 102:1 suggest they should do?
options: Pray and cry out to God
questions.correctAnswer: Pray and cry out to God
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:1 encourages, 'Hear my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee,' suggesting the importance of prayer in times of distress.

questions.question: Should one hide their face from God in times of trouble according to Psalms 102:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:2 requests, 'Hide not thy face from me in the day when I am in trouble,' indicating that one should seek God's presence rather than retreat.

questions.question: Is it true that the psalmist feels like he is consumed like smoke in Psalms 102:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:3 states, 'For my days are consumed like smoke,' expressing the psalmist's feeling of transience and despair.

questions.question: Is it false that the psalmist only feels sorrow for himself according to Psalms 102:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:4 reveals that 'My heart is smitten, and withered like grass,' indicating deep sorrow affecting him profoundly, not just self-focused.

questions.question: Is it false that the psalmist feels abandoned and alone in Psalms 102:7?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 102:7, the psalmist states, 'I watch, and am as a sparrow alone upon the house top,' clearly expressing feelings of isolation and abandonment.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 102 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 102.

questions.question: According to Psalms 102:21, what is declared in Zion?
options: The name of the LORD and his praise
questions.correctAnswer: The name of the LORD and his praise
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:21 states, 'To declare the name of the LORD in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem;' indicating the declaration of God's name and praise specifically in Zion.

questions.question: In Psalms 102:22, when do the kingdoms serve the LORD?
options: When the people are gathered together
At the fall of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: When the people are gathered together
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:22 reads, 'When the people are gathered together, and the kingdoms, to serve the LORD,' showing that service to the LORD occurs at the gathering of people and kingdoms.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say God did to his strength and days in Psalms 102:23?
options: Weakened his strength and shortened his days
Increased his strength and lengthened his days
Healed his strength and restored his days
Tested his strength and multiplied his days
questions.correctAnswer: Weakened his strength and shortened his days
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:23 says, 'He weakened my strength in the way; he shortened my days,' indicating a decline in both strength and lifespan.

questions.question: What plea does the psalmist make to God in Psalms 102:24?
options: Take me not away in the midst of my days
questions.correctAnswer: Take me not away in the midst of my days
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:24 states, 'I said, O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days: thy years are throughout all generations,' expressing a plea not to be taken away prematurely.

questions.question: According to Psalms 102:25, what has God laid from ancient times?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:25 states, 'Of old hast thou laid the foundation of the earth: and the heavens are the work of thy hands,' emphasizing God's role as Creator.

questions.question: What contrast is made between God and creation in Psalms 102:26-27?
options: Creation will perish, but God endures forever
Creation and God both are eternal
Creation is eternal, but God changes
Both creation and God will perish
questions.correctAnswer: Creation will perish, but God endures forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:26-27 explain, 'They shall perish, but thou shalt endure... But thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end,' highlighting God's eternal nature contrasted with the perishability of creation.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'yesod' in Psalms 102:25 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'yesod' (יסוד) in Psalms 102:25 means 'foundation,' referring to the foundational laying of the earth by God.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Psalms 102:26 when it says, 'all of them shall wax old like a garment; as a vesture shalt thou change them'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:26 uses a simile comparing creation aging to a garment growing old, using 'like' to make the comparison explicit.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's unchanging nature found in Psalms 102:27?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 13:8 states, 'Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and today, and forever,' echoing the unchanging nature of God described in Psalms 102:27.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of God's eternal reign and creation as described in Psalms 102:25-27?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:28 speaks of God as the Creator who never grows tired or weary, connecting closely with Psalms 102:25-27's emphasis on God's eternal and unchanging nature.

questions.question: What is the verse immediately preceding Psalms 102:21?
options: Psalms 102:20 - To hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death;
Psalms 102:19 - For he hath looked down from the height of his sanctuary;
Psalms 102:18 - This shall be written for the generation to come:
Psalms 102:22 - When the people are gathered together, and the kingdoms, to serve the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 102:20 - To hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death;
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:20 directly precedes verse 21, describing God hearing the groaning of prisoners, setting the context for declaring God's name in Zion in 102:21.

questions.question: How does Psalms 102:28 serve as a conclusion to the themes in the final section of the psalm?
options: It affirms the continuation of the descendants of God's servants
It calls for immediate judgment on enemies
It recounts the historical sins of Israel
It prophesies a coming Messiah explicitly
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the continuation of the descendants of God's servants
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:28 concludes the section by saying, 'The children of thy servants shall continue, and their seed shall be established before thee,' emphasizing continuity and hope.

questions.question: What poetic parallelism is evident between Psalms 102:3 and Psalms 102:11?
options: Both verses use similes comparing the psalmist's life to smoke and shadows
Both verses use hyperbole to exaggerate suffering
Both verses describe God's everlasting mercy
Both verses focus on the joy of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Both verses use similes comparing the psalmist's life to smoke and shadows
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:3 says, 'my days are consumed like smoke,' and 102:11 says, 'My days are like a shadow that declineth,' both employing similes to express transience.

questions.question: What typological significance might Psalms 102:13's phrase 'Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Zion' have in New Testament theology?
options: It foreshadows Christ's resurrection and mercy toward His people
It predicts the building of Solomon's temple
It refers exclusively to the Exodus event
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ's resurrection and mercy toward His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:13's call for God to 'arise' and show mercy is often seen typologically as foreshadowing Christ's resurrection and redemptive mercy in the New Testament.

questions.question: The statement 'Thy years are throughout all generations' in Psalms 102:24 emphasizes which theological concept?
options: The establishment of the Mosaic covenant
questions.explanation: In Psalms 102:24, 'thy years are throughout all generations' highlights God's eternal existence beyond human lifespan limits.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 102 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 102 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 102:27 teach about God's nature?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:27 states, 'But thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end,' teaching God's immutability and eternality.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 102:12 teach regarding God's relationship to history and covenant?
options: God endures forever and is remembered throughout all generations
God's covenant is temporary and conditional
God is forgotten by future generations
God's presence is limited to a single generation
questions.correctAnswer: God endures forever and is remembered throughout all generations
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:12 declares, 'But thou, O LORD, shalt endure for ever; and thy remembrance unto all generations,' emphasizing God's eternal covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine providence does Psalms 102:23 teach?
options: God weakens human strength and shortens days as part of His sovereign will
God allows humans to act independently without intervention
God grants unlimited strength and lifespan to the faithful
God's providence is random and chaotic
questions.correctAnswer: God weakens human strength and shortens days as part of His sovereign will
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:23 says, 'He weakened my strength in the way; he shortened my days,' which expresses God's sovereign control over human life and suffering.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 102:19 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:19 says, 'For he hath looked down from the height of his sanctuary; from heaven did the LORD behold the earth,' showing God's all-seeing, omniscient nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 102:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:17 states, 'He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer,' demonstrating God's mercy toward the afflicted.

questions.question: How does Psalms 102:25–26 prepare for New Testament themes of Christ's eternal nature and creation?
options: By affirming God's role as creator whose works will perish but who endures forever
By denying God's involvement in creation
By teaching that creation is eternal alongside God
By emphasizing human dominion over creation
questions.correctAnswer: By affirming God's role as creator whose works will perish but who endures forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:25–26 describes God laying the earth's foundation and the heavens as His workmanship, which will perish, but God endures eternally, prefiguring Christ's eternal creative role (cf. John 1:3).

questions.question: How does Psalms 102:13 connect to the messianic hope and eschatological restoration in Scripture?
options: It speaks of God's arising to show mercy upon Zion at the appointed time
It describes the destruction of Zion without hope
It denies any future restoration of Israel
It predicts the permanent exile of Zion
questions.correctAnswer: It speaks of God's arising to show mercy upon Zion at the appointed time
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:13 declares, 'Thou shalt arise, and have mercy upon Zion: for the time to favour her, yea, the set time, is come,' connecting to the eschatological restoration of Israel and messianic fulfillment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 102:12 and 102:27 teach about God's nature?
options: God is eternal, unchanging, and remembered across all generations
God is temporary and subject to change
God is forgotten by future generations
God changes according to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God is eternal, unchanging, and remembered across all generations
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 27 together affirm God's eternal existence and immutability: 'O LORD, shalt endure for ever' and 'But thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end.'

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 102:17 and 102:20 teach about God's care for the afflicted?
options: God hears and regards the prayers of the destitute and frees those appointed to death
God ignores the suffering of the poor
God punishes the afflicted without mercy
God is indifferent to human prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and regards the prayers of the destitute and frees those appointed to death
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:17 says God 'will regard the prayer of the destitute,' and 102:20 states He hears prisoners and frees those doomed to death, showing divine compassion and intervention.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 102:23 and 102:24 teach about human frailty and God's eternal nature?
options: Human life is limited and frail, but God's years are eternal
Human life and God's nature are equally temporary
God shortens human days arbitrarily without purpose
Human strength is unlimited by God's will
questions.correctAnswer: Human life is limited and frail, but God's years are eternal
questions.explanation: Verses 23 and 24 contrast the psalmist's shortened days and weakened strength with God's eternal years, emphasizing human frailty versus divine eternality.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 102:25-28 teaches that God is subject to change like creation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God is unchanging and eternal, whereas creation is transient and subject to change
God changes as often as creation changes
God is created along with the heavens and earth
Creation and God share the same temporal limitations
questions.correctAnswer: God is unchanging and eternal, whereas creation is transient and subject to change
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:25-28 contrasts the perishable creation with the eternal, unchanging God: 'They shall perish... but thou shalt endure... But thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end.'

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 102:18 teach about the transmission of divine praise to future generations?
options: God's praise is recorded and will be declared to future generations
Praise of God is limited to the current generation
Future generations will reject God's praise
God's works remain hidden from all generations
questions.correctAnswer: God's praise is recorded and will be declared to future generations
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:18 states, 'This shall be written for the generation to come: and the people which shall be created shall praise the LORD,' affirming the continuity of divine worship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 102:22?
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:22 says, 'When the people are gathered together, and the kingdoms, to serve the LORD,' demonstrating God's universal sovereign rule over all nations.

questions.question: How does Psalms 102:9 contribute to the theological understanding of repentance and lament?
options: It expresses deep sorrow and mourning as part of penitential lament
It denies any emotional response to sin
It portrays joy and celebration in suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses deep sorrow and mourning as part of penitential lament
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:9 says, 'For I have eaten ashes like bread, and mingled my drink with weeping,' depicting profound grief and repentance in lament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 102:1 and 102:17 teach about prayer and God's response to affliction?
options: God hears the cries of the afflicted and answers their prayers
Prayer is ineffective in times of trouble
God despises the prayers of the afflicted
questions.correctAnswer: God hears the cries of the afflicted and answers their prayers
questions.explanation: Psalms 102:1 calls for God to hear the prayer of the afflicted, and 102:17 assures that God 'will regard the prayer of the destitute,' affirming divine responsiveness.
